title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp.107-110). X is a smooth multiplicity (orbifold/stack), in the intended application \bar M_{g,ν}, with a normal-crossings boundary divisor D. D_d is the normalized codimension-d stratum: a point of D_d is a point of X together with a choice of d local branches of D through it. D'_d = \tilde D_d is the principal S_d-torsor over D_d of orderings of those d branches. Grothendieck writes \mathfrak G_d, so (\mathfrak G_d)_{D_d} is the constant group S_d over D_d. A 'type' is a finite poset J with a codimension function c and a least element e_J of codimension d. D_J is the multiplicity classifying a point of D_d together with a configuration of strata through it, indexed by J and compatible with order and codimension. The previous page notes that D_J → X is a local immersion of codim d, that D_{{•}} = D_d, and that the two-element flag (d, 1) gives \tilde D_d.

This page.
(154) H(J) is the finite set of codim-compatible order-embeddings J → P(I_d)^op, where I_d = {1,…,d} and codim = cardinality. This is the local model: the strata through a point of codim d correspond to subsets of the set of d branches, ordered by reverse inclusion. Necessarily e_J ↦ I_d.
(155) S_d acts on H(J) through its action on I_d, and there is a canonical isomorphism D_J ≅ D'_d ∧^{S_d} H(J). This is the contracted product (associated bundle) of the branch-ordering torsor with the finite S_d-set H(J). It reduces the whole family of strata-type multiplicities D_J to the single pair (D_d, D'_d) plus finite combinatorics.
(156)-(157) A codim-compatible embedding f: J' → J induces a contravariant morphism D_J → D_{J'} (forgetting part of the configuration). Grothendieck then asks which extra data on the pairs (D_d, D'_d), 'if needed', would make this functoriality explicit through (155).

The difficulty is when f does not preserve least elements. Then D_{J'} lives over D_{d'} with d' < d, and H(J) → H(J') by restriction is not an S_d-map between sets of the right shape. The next page resolves this through the flag multiplicities D_{d,d'} ≅ D'_d ∧^{S_d} Π_{d'}(I_d), where Π_{d'} means subsets of cardinality d', and through the evaluation map H(J) → Π_{d'}(I_d), h ↦ h(x). So the missing gluing data are the maps D_{d,d'} → D_{d'} relating different codimensions.

Purpose: build a functorial combinatorial description of the stratification at infinity of \bar M_{g,ν}, as a diagram indexed by types J, to study the 'structure at infinity' (boundary, tubular neighbourhoods, Teichmüller-tower combinatorics).
errors: No real error. One minor point: (155) presupposes that J has a least element e_J, which was imposed on the previous page.
'Plongement' should be read as an injective, order- and codim-compatible map. Since codim is cardinality, injectivity is automatic only on elements of equal codimension; this is harmless.
Naive functoriality via (155) fails when f(e_{J'}) ≠ e_J, as Grothendieck himself recognises; the gap is addressed on the next page.

ideas.what: Strata of a normal-crossings divisor described locally by subsets of the set of branches, with the S_d-torsor of branch orderings over the normalized codim-d stratum
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorics of snc/nc stratifications; monodromy torsor of branches; generalized cone complex / Kato fan of a log smooth pair
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Deligne, Hodge II for normal crossings); log-geometric form by Kato (1989-94); Abramovich-Caporaso-Payne (2015) for \bar M_{g,n}
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck–Murre (LNM 208, 1971) treats normal-crossings divisors and tame fundamental groups; unsure about this exact formulation

ideas.what: Strata-type multiplicity D_J as the contracted product of D'_d with the finite S_d-set of codim-compatible embeddings J → P(I_d)^op
ideas.modern_name: Associated bundle / contracted product; strata indexed by poset types (analogue of stable-graph strata \bar M_Γ = (∏ \bar M_{g_v,n_v})/Aut Γ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard torsor technique; stratification of \bar M_{g,n} by dual graphs (Deligne–Mumford, Knudsen)

ideas.what: Contravariant functoriality J ↦ D_J along codim-compatible embeddings, and the question of what extra data on the (D_d, D'_d) makes it explicit
ideas.modern_name: Diagram of strata indexed by a category of types; Artin fan / cone stack of a log structure (Abramovich–Chen–Marcus–Wise; Cavalieri–Chan–Ulirsch–Wise)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Abramovich–Wise et al. (2010s); cone stacks of Cavalieri–Chan–Ulirsch–Wise (2020)

missed.claim: Grothendieck organizes the boundary strata of \bar M_{g,ν} as a functor on a category of codim-weighted posets. Each value is the contracted product of one torsor with a finite combinatorial set, and the gluing data across codimensions are sought explicitly. This is close in spirit to the later Artin fan / cone stack formalism for the boundary of \bar M_{g,n}, but is phrased purely in terms of the normal-crossings divisor, with no log structure.
missed.quote: on a un iso. can. de D-multiplicités (155) D_J ≃ \tilde D_d ∧^{(\mathfrak G_d)_{D_d}} H(J)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: an early, independent anticipation of describing boundary combinatorics functorially (cone stacks, tropical moduli). It is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard normal-crossings combinatorics, packaged with torsors and contracted products. The functorial indexing by codim-weighted posets is a mildly interesting anticipation of later cone-stack ideas, but it is routine for a specialist.
transcription_corrections: In (155) the group is written as the subscript (\mathfrak G_d)_{D_d} under the contracted-product sign, i.e. the constant group S_d over D_d. Over \tilde D_d there is an inserted mark ('ns' / prime), consistent with the D'_d of the neighbouring pages.
In the line after (157), the bracketed pair reads (D_d, \tilde D_d) or (D_d, D'_d), with an overwritten prime.

Last lines: 'Considérons' is struck and replaced by 'Comme la'; the struck line reads 'd'abord le plus petit élément e_J de e'; the final line reads 'dépendance fonctorielle en J pour les iso' (continued on the next page).
